newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Supersol may buy Shekem supermarkets.
newsitem.headline: Supersol may buy Shekem supermarkets.

text.p: Supersol Ltd is exploring acquiring the supermarket business of retailer Shekem Ltd, a Supersol executive said on Sunday.

"I can say one thing: Shekem proposed to number of parties the possibility of selling its food business. We are making clarifications in connection with this offer," Yacov Ginzburg, Supersol's vice president for marketing and purchasing, told Reuters.

On Sunday morning Shekem told the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange it was exploring the sale of its supermasrket business and was in contact with a number of unnamed parties in the food retail sector. A spokeswoman refused to provide any further details.

Some newspaper reports said Blue Square Chain Stores Properties & Investments Ltd was also weighing the offer, but a spokeswoman was not immediately available for comment. Blue Square is a subsidiary of Blue Square Israel Ltd.

Shekem, controlled by Elco Holdings Ltd, operates about 30 supermarkets, but its main business is in general department stores. The company is undergoing an overhaul, cutting expenses and giving its department stores a more fashionable image.
In the meantime, Shekem has experienced chronic losses. In the first nine months of 1996, it reported a 9.6 million shekel loss on revenues of 854.5 million shekels.
In its statement, Shekem said the sale of its supermarkets was in the framework of the reorganisation.
Ginzburg noted that Shekem's supermarket business comprises several divisions and it was not yet clear what was being offered for sale.

Supersol and Blue Square dominate the retail food sector, but newspaper reports said the Industry and Trade Ministry's antitrust authority had approved the possible sale of Shekem's business to either one of the two.
Yoram Turbowicz, the commissioner for restrictive business practices, was not available for comment.
